title: How the AmFest suit-fit explanation was disputed
summary: Tracks Erika Kirk’s quoted explanation that only the sparkly suit fit and Owens’s later rebuttal using other public outfits; it does not establish what fit on the day.

milestones.label: Suit fit explained
milestones.proposition: Erika, quoted through the profile, explains the sparkly AmFest suit as the only clothing that fit and says outsiders see only half the picture.
milestones.review_note: Reviewed 1250–1339s. The quoted explanation is a counteraccount to public outfit criticism, not an independently established wardrobe fact.
milestones.statement_text: Erika Kirk said people see her sparkly suit on stage but do not know it was “the only thing that fit,” adding that everyone gets a half picture.
milestones.speaker: Erika Kirk

evidence.text: Erika Kirk said people see her sparkly suit on stage but do not know it was “the only thing that fit,” adding that everyone gets a half picture.

milestones.label: Fit explanation disputed
milestones.proposition: Owens rejects Erika’s only-fitting-suit explanation, citing other outfits from public appearances as possible alternatives.
milestones.review_note: Reviewed 1338–1476s and supporting statements-3eee2eefeac2 and 0d1b5ee73fb6. Her I feel and I do not believe qualifiers remain material. Pictures from other days do not independently establish what fit on the AmFest day; the December opening-date discrepancy is not resolved by this argument.
milestones.statement_text: Owens said, “I feel like Erika Kirk is not telling the truth” that the glittery suit was the only thing that fit, and said she did not believe it because other options were available.
milestones.speaker: Candace Owens

evidence.text: Owens said, “I feel like Erika Kirk is not telling the truth” that the glittery suit was the only thing that fit, and said she did not believe it because other options were available.
evidence.speaker: Candace Owens
excerpts: So I just, I feel like Erica (Erika Kirk) is not telling the truth when she says that was the only thing that fit her. That, I, that, I don't believe that. I feel like that's dumb and she had some other options that were available, and it doesn't, it never feels like a necessary lie.
